rules.title: Santa Ana Rent Stabilization Ordinance
rules.requirement: Annual rent increases are capped at the lower of 3% or 80% of the 12-month CPI change; no increase if CPI is negative. The current allowable increase is 2.87% for 9/1/2026 through 8/31/2027. Landlords must give written notice of the ordinance at lease start or with any rent increase notice.
rules.quoted_span: Increase in residential rents are limited to the lower of 3% per year, or 80% of the percent change in the Consumer Price Index over the most recent 12-month period
rules.key_value: Lesser of 3% or 80% of CPI change; 2.87% for 9/1/2026-8/31/2027
rules.effective_date_note: Official city page states the ordinances are not effective until November 19, 2021; adoption date not given.
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential buildings constructed on or before February 1, 1995.
rules.exemptions: Residential buildings constructed after February 1, 1995; mobile home spaces offered for rent after January 1, 1990. Owners may petition the City Manager for relief for a fair and reasonable return.
rules.interaction: Local cap governs in place of the state Tenant Protection Act cap. Allowable increase is published by June 30 each year, effective September 1.

unverifiable_exemptions: mobile home spaces offered for rent after January 1, 1990

rules.review_note: Ordinance section number not stated in documents; cited by name. Current 2.87% figure from D084.

rules.title: Santa Ana Just Cause Eviction Ordinance
rules.requirement: After 30 days of tenancy, an owner cannot end a tenancy without a just cause stated in a written notice. For at-fault causes the owner must first give notice and a chance to cure. For no-fault terminations the owner must give 3 months of relocation assistance or waive the final 3 months of rent.
rules.citation: Santa Ana Just Cause Eviction Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: After 30 days, an owner shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in a written notice
rules.key_value: Just cause required after 30 days; 3 months relocation assistance or rent waiver for no-fault
rules.effective_date_note: Official city page states the ordinances are not effective until November 19, 2021.
rules.coverage_conditions: Private residential rentals not within the listed exemptions.
rules.exemptions: Housing produced in the last 15 years; deed-restricted affordable housing; hotel and transient occupancy; hospital and care facilities; dormitories; other shared living quarters.
rules.interaction: Local ordinance governs in place of the state just-cause law where both apply.

unverifiable_exemptions: dormitories and other shared living quarters

rules.review_note: Ordinance section number not stated in documents; cited by name.

rules.title: Santa Ana ban on algorithmic rent-setting software
rules.requirement: Landlords may not use, and vendors may not sell, license or provide, algorithmic rent-setting software that uses nonpublic competitor data for Santa Ana residential rentals. Tenants can sue for injunctive relief, damages, or civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation per month plus attorney's fees.
rules.quoted_span: Ordinance NS-3090 prohibits specified anticompetitive automated rent price-fixing; private tenant claims and up to $1,000 per violation and per month
rules.key_value: Ban on algorithmic devices using nonpublic competitor data; up to $1,000 per violation per month
rules.penalty: Up to $1,000 per violation and per month; injunctive relief, damages, attorney's fees
rules.effective_date_note: Law-firm alert states effective April 2, 2026; first reading Feb. 17, 2026, final vote reported for March 3, 2026.
rules.exemptions: Pricing software relying solely on publicly available data, aggregate historical data, or tools used to comply with affordable housing program requirements.

unverifiable_exemptions: software relying solely on public data, aggregate historical data, or affordable housing compliance tools

rules.review_note: Only secondary sources available; no official ordinance text provided.

parsed.notes: Santa Ana: rent stabilization, just cause (with relocation), and algorithmic ban NS-3090. No city-level documents on deposits, screening fees, or screening restrictions were provided, so no findings for them.
